page.text:
The elementary constructors established in previous sections—pairing,
union, and power set—form only the scaffolding of modern set theory. To
develop higher mathematics, analysis, and transfinite ordinal arithmetic,
Zermelo--Fraenkel set theory incorporates powerful principles governing
how predicates select elements from existing sets, how functional
assignments generate new collections, and how ill-founded pathologies are
excluded.

Because first-order logic cannot quantify over arbitrary properties or
predicates, principles such as Separation and Replacement cannot be
expressed as single axioms. Instead, they are formulated as *axiom
schemas*—infinite families of axioms, supplying one formal postulate for
every well-formed formula $\varphi$ in the language $\mathcal{L}_{\in}$.
